title: Pruebas de datos, propiedades e integración
review_contracts: PYARCANA — MODO REVISOR ESCÉPTICO Y ANTI-COMPLACENCIA
Solarized Website Content Comprehension Auditor & Rewriter

prior_audit.method: Direct fetch of audit/lessons-only/sections/S28.json returned 404 before creation.

learner_entry_state.credit_rule: Only prior concepts adjudicated USABLE count as learned.
learner_entry_state.critical_dependency_warning: S26 and S27 remain REPAIR_REQUIRED. S28 must not assume N2/CF-2 passed or that print-only pseudo-tests from S27 are executable evidence.
required_regression_carry_forward: final approval must bind exact draft hash and recipients
E2E promotion must derive from observed manifests

roadmap_expectation.T1: properties/invariants/case generation plus idempotence, symmetry and metamorphic tests
roadmap_expectation.T2: schema/data-quality contracts plus golden datasets, drift and reconciliation
roadmap_expectation.T3: HTTP/DB/clock doubles plus contract tests without over-mocking
roadmap_expectation.T4: integration/E2E/testcontainers plus flakes, determinism and CI
roadmap_expectation.gate: suite finds encoding, cardinality, ordering, timeout and resumption errors with minimal synthetic fixtures

live_site.evidence: Public card exposes Section 28 'Propiedades e integración' with the same tagline about encoding/cardinality/order/timeout/resumption. Render-only defects were not invented.

external_research: Hypothesis 6.167.1: property-based testing generates examples from strategies, shrinks failures, persists/reuses failing examples; property-based testing is an addition to unit tests, not always a replacement.
Hypothesis reproduction: falsifying examples/example database/reproduce_failure are primary mechanisms; a seed is not normally the sole exact failure artifact.
pytest current docs: real fixtures are dependency-injected and support function/class/module/package/session scopes plus yield teardown; monkeypatch is a scoped supported fixture.
Python unittest.mock docs: autospec/spec can detect fake/mock API drift and wrong signatures.
Testcontainers: containers provide throwaway real service types and avoid semantic gaps of in-memory substitutes; same type/version/config still has to be chosen explicitly.
Python str.casefold is more aggressive than lower; it removes case distinctions such as ß→ss but does not perform Unicode normalization.
Python random docs recommend independent Random instances when state isolation matters.
IANA reserved example domains do not include example.pe.

checks: validate_record accepts id='   ', email='@', score=True with zero errors despite claimed type/domain contracts.
sim_token('', '') returns 1.0, treating two missing names as perfect similarity.
casefold+split normalize does not unify NFC 'José' and NFD 'José', contradicting the later integration requirement to unify NFC/NFD.
T1-A/T1-B/T2/T3/T4 theory snippets predominantly print booleans/results; several can report false/wrong values without failing pytest because they are not pytest tests.
golden reconcile(old,new,approved=True) only returns the string 'updated'; it neither persists a new golden nor records reviewer/timestamp/note/hash.
FakeHTTP only returns status/body; no retry/timeout behavior is executed despite prose claiming 503 retry evidence.
integration_sqlite returns entities/pairs/encoding but has no assertions and does not test ordering, timeout, checkpoint or restart.
flaky_bad is effectively always true: datetime.now().microsecond >= 0 is tautological and random.random()>0 fails only at the exact zero value.

findings.title: KNOWN_S26_REGRESSIONS_IGNORED_AT_LEVEL3_ENTRY
findings.evidence: S27 carry-forward requires a minimal inherited regression pack for cycle/HITL/idempotency/restart/compensation/E2E; S28 theory starts new ER properties without those tests.
findings.impact: The course teaches risk-first testing while ignoring the highest-known regression risks at the level boundary.
findings.attack: A new suite can go green while the known S26 critical controls remain broken.
findings.defense: S28 is scoped to QA of CP-N3-A rather than retrofitting all Level-2 defects.

findings.title: NON_RESERVED_EXAMPLE_PE_REINTRODUCED
findings.evidence: Fixtures and FakeHTTP use @example.pe / https://example.pe/er.
findings.impact: A supposedly synthetic namespace can become routable when tests later cross real HTTP/email boundaries.
findings.attack: IANA reserves example.com/example.org and special-use test domains, not example.pe.
findings.defense: No canonical snippet performs a real request to that URL today.

findings.title: SYSTEMATIC_PYTEST_PROMISE_STILL_REPLACED_BY_PRINTS
findings.evidence: Theory snippets compute idempotent_ok/symmetric/meta/dirty/drift/contract/encoding/stable and print them; they are not collected pytest assertions.
findings.impact: A broken contract can print False and the process can still exit successfully.
findings.attack: Roadmap says from S27 pytest is systematic and S28 gate is an executable suite.
findings.defense: I Do later contains some test_* functions and the theory code is illustrative.

findings.title: PROPERTY_FIGURE_FALSELY_NESTS_EXAMPLE_TESTS_INSIDE_PROPERTY_TESTS
findings.evidence: Figure alt describes property-based as a containing region around example-based tests.
findings.impact: Learner may infer property tests subsume example tests instead of complementing them.
findings.attack: Current Hypothesis docs explicitly say property-based testing is a powerful addition and not always a replacement.
findings.defense: The figure likely intends to convey broader input exploration, not formal set inclusion.

findings.title: PROPERTY_QUANTIFIER_OMITS_INPUT_DOMAIN
findings.evidence: Opening says a property must hold siempre / sin importar la entrada.
findings.impact: Learner may apply invariants to invalid inputs outside the declared strategy/preconditions.
findings.attack: Properties quantify over a defined domain/strategy, not arbitrary Python values.
findings.defense: Subsequent text mentions strategies and generated input spaces.

findings.title: HYPOTHESIS_REPRODUCTION_MISSTATED_AS_EXACT_SEED
findings.evidence: Opening claims that on a counterexample the tool returns the exact seed to reproduce it.
findings.impact: Creates the wrong failure-reproduction model for Hypothesis.
findings.attack: Hypothesis primarily reports falsifying examples, uses its example database and can emit reproduce_failure; seed is not normally the sole artifact.
findings.defense: Hypothesis does expose seed controls and can print seeds in some situations.

findings.title: HUNDREDS_OF_INPUTS_FALSE_PRECISION
findings.evidence: Opening says the machine generates hundreds of inputs.
findings.impact: Turns configurable test effort into a pseudo-guaranteed quantity.
findings.attack: Current Hypothesis default max_examples is 100 and actual execution can differ due to phases/filtering/settings.
findings.defense: The word is illustrative rather than a formal guarantee.

findings.title: T1A_INVARIANT_FAILURE_DOES_NOT_FAIL_THE_SUITE
findings.evidence: invariants_gen.py accumulates bad cases and prints idempotent_ok instead of asserting len(bad)==0.
findings.impact: A discovered counterexample can leave the script exit code green.
findings.attack: This defeats the section's executable-contract gate.
findings.defense: The boolean makes the result visible to a reader.

findings.title: GLOBAL_FIXED_RANDOM_SEED_BOTH_NARROWS_EXPLORATION_AND_MUTATES_SHARED_STATE
findings.evidence: random.seed(42) is called at module level and stable() reseeds the module RNG.
findings.impact: Tests repeatedly explore the same small sample and can couple other tests through global RNG state.
findings.attack: Use random.Random(seed) for isolation and property tooling/example database for broader exploration.
findings.defense: Fixed seeds provide deterministic CI and reproducibility for a beginner lab.

findings.title: RANDOM_WITHOUT_SEED_EQ_FLAKE_OVERGENERALIZATION
findings.evidence: Callout says Random sin seed en CI es flake.
findings.impact: Conflates nondeterministic input generation with intermittent test failure.
findings.attack: A randomized test can remain correct if failures are reproducible/captured; a flake is intermittent pass/fail without code change.
findings.defense: Uncontrolled randomness is a common cause of flaky behavior.

findings.title: EMPTY_EMPTY_NAMES_SCORE_AS_PERFECT_MATCH
findings.evidence: sim_token returns 1.0 when both token sets are empty and the canonical pairs include ('','').
findings.impact: Missing data becomes strong positive identity evidence.
findings.attack: Two unknown names should not create perfect evidence unless the contract explicitly defines a special non-evidentiary sentinel.
findings.defense: Mathematically some Jaccard conventions define empty-empty similarity as 1.

findings.title: DIRECTED_EDIT_DISTANCE_EXAMPLE_MISLEADS
findings.evidence: Callout contrasts test_jaccard_is_symmetric with test_edit_distance_directed.
findings.impact: Learner may believe standard edit/Levenshtein distance is inherently directed.
findings.attack: Standard Levenshtein with symmetric costs is symmetric; direction requires a deliberately asymmetric cost/algorithm contract.
findings.defense: The text says algunas distancias dirigidas rather than all edit distances.

findings.title: CASEFOLD_ONLY_CASING_ABSOLUTE_IS_TECHNICALLY_FALSE
findings.evidence: Text says casefold normaliza mayúsculas y minúsculas, y solo eso.
findings.impact: Creates an inaccurate Unicode model.
findings.attack: Python documents casefold as more aggressive than lower, e.g. ß→ss; the correct limit is that it is not Unicode normalization.
findings.defense: The intended warning—casefold does not normalize NFC/NFD—is correct.

findings.title: METAMORPHIC_TEST_TESTS_DUPLICATED_INLINE_EXPRESSION_NOT_PRODUCTION_NORMALIZER
findings.evidence: meta_ok repeats join/split/casefold expressions on both sides instead of calling the normalize API used by the ER pipeline.
findings.impact: Production normalize can be broken while this property remains green.
findings.attack: Properties must target the actual public behavior under test.
findings.defense: The expression demonstrates the mathematical relation in minimal code.

findings.title: SCHEMA_VALIDATOR_DOES_NOT_ENFORCE_ITS_DECLARED_TYPES_AND_DOMAINS
findings.evidence: validate_record accepts id='   ', email='@', score=True and accepts numeric strings through float coercion.
findings.impact: Rows can satisfy the regression contract while violating the stated schema.
findings.attack: A schema contract should distinguish type validation from intentional coercion and reject whitespace-only identifiers/degenerate addresses.
findings.defense: The validator is explicitly didactic and minimal.

findings.title: BATCH_QUALITY_CLAIMS_ARE_NOT_TESTABLE_BY_ROW_VALIDATOR
findings.evidence: Prose names unique ids, pair cardinality and UTF-8 legibility; validate_record only sees one decoded dict.
findings.impact: Core quality invariants can never fail in the demonstrated contract.
findings.attack: Uniqueness/cardinality require batch context and encoding requires byte/decode boundary evidence.
findings.defense: Later integration code covers pair count and Unicode normalization partially.

findings.title: FAIL_CLOSED_BATCH_STOP_EXISTS_ONLY_IN_PROSE
findings.evidence: Theory says a broken batch stops with report; code only builds report and prints dirty_n.
findings.impact: The learner sees detection but not enforcement.
findings.attack: A regression gate must raise/fail or return an explicit blocking result consumed by the caller.
findings.defense: The snippet focuses on the validator rather than orchestration.

findings.title: GOLDEN_IS_NOT_A_VERSIONED_PERSISTED_ARTIFACT
findings.evidence: golden_drift.py constructs two in-memory dicts and compares them.
findings.impact: The section does not demonstrate the file/version/change-review properties that define a golden snapshot.
findings.attack: No JSON/CSV file is loaded, hashed, committed or diffed.
findings.defense: In-memory dicts isolate the drift/reconcile concept from file I/O.

findings.title: GOLDEN_APPROVAL_IS_AN_UNAUTHENTICATED_BOOLEAN_AND_RECONCILE_DOES_NOT_RECONCILE
findings.evidence: reconcile(old,new,approved=True) returns 'updated' but records no reviewer/timestamp/note/hash and persists nothing.
findings.impact: A caller can self-approve a regression and no auditable golden changes.
findings.attack: This contradicts the paragraph requiring human review plus change note.
findings.defense: approved is a didactic placeholder for a later workflow.

findings.title: RAW_GOLDEN_EQUALITY_CONFUSES_ORDER_NOISE_WITH_SEMANTIC_DRIFT
findings.evidence: golden != current compares list order directly while prose identifies ordering as possible noise.
findings.impact: Harmless ordering changes can block CI or be misclassified as matcher drift.
findings.attack: Canonicalize unordered pair sets and controlled numeric tolerances before semantic diff.
findings.defense: The supplied minimal fixture preserves order so the immediate example is deterministic.

findings.title: DRIFT_TERM_OVERLOADED_WITH_SNAPSHOT_DIFFERENCE
findings.evidence: Any golden diff is called drift.
findings.impact: Prepares confusion with later data/model drift where the measured phenomenon is distribution/performance change over time.
findings.attack: Use golden_diff/snapshot_diff here and reserve drift or qualify it explicitly.
findings.defense: The paragraph defines its local meaning before use.

findings.title: 503_RETRY_AND_TIMEOUT_CLAIM_NOT_EXECUTED
findings.evidence: T3-A says the pattern demonstrates retries on 503; FakeHTTP only returns a dict containing status and no service/retry function is called.
findings.impact: A learner may mistake controllable fake response data for tested retry behavior.
findings.attack: Inject a sequence of 503/200 or timeout exception and assert attempts/backoff/result.
findings.defense: The subtopic's primary construct is doubles, not retry policy itself.

findings.title: FAKE_HTTP_CAN_DRIFT_FROM_REAL_CLIENT_CONTRACT
findings.evidence: FakeHTTP invents get_json(url) and arbitrary response shape without interface/spec checking.
findings.impact: Production client signature/shape can change while fake-based tests remain green.
findings.attack: Use a Protocol/interface, contract test, or autospec for mocks where appropriate.
findings.defense: A hand-written fake can intentionally implement a stable application-owned adapter interface.

findings.title: MOCKS_DEFINED_BUT_NO_ACTUAL_MOCK_INTERACTION_TEST_IS_SHOWN
findings.evidence: T3-A defines Mock/Fake/Stub, but canonical executable demonstrates only hand-written fakes/dicts.
findings.impact: The learner cannot practice when interaction assertions are useful or risky.
findings.attack: Show one autospecced interaction boundary and contrast it with fake state-based testing.
findings.defense: Learning outcome emphasizes controlled doubles broadly, not unittest.mock specifically.

findings.title: GLOBAL_PATCHING_DISMISSED_TOO_BROADLY
findings.evidence: Callout says no parches globales salvo legado.
findings.impact: Learner may avoid safe scoped environment/module patches even when dependency injection is impractical.
findings.attack: pytest monkeypatch is a supported fixture that restores changes automatically after the test.
findings.defense: Dependency injection is generally the more explicit design for application-owned dependencies.

findings.title: TEXT_NORMALIZATION_CONTRACT_CONTRADICTS_ITS_OWN_NFC_NFD_REQUIREMENT
findings.evidence: T3-B normalize uses casefold+split only; T4-A says NFC/NFD must be unified with unicodedata.normalize.
findings.impact: Visually equivalent names can fail match in one canonical layer and pass in another.
findings.attack: Runtime check: 'José' NFC and its NFD form remain unequal after casefold+split.
findings.defense: T4-A introduces the additional normalization specifically at integration time.

findings.title: FAKE_NETWORK_OR_DISK_HEURISTIC_TOO_BROAD
findings.evidence: T3-B says if code talks to network or disk, fake the boundary.
findings.impact: Learner may mock away the filesystem/database integration behavior the test is supposed to verify.
findings.attack: Choose doubles based on test scope; tmp_path/SQLite/Testcontainers should remain real when that boundary is the construct.
findings.defense: The surrounding paragraph is explicitly warning against over-mocking and later demonstrates real SQLite.

findings.title: INTEGRATION_DEMO_HAS_NO_ASSERTIONS_OR_PYTEST_GATE
findings.evidence: integration_sqlite.py returns n/pairs/encoding_ok and prints them.
findings.impact: A wrong row count or pair result can still produce exit code 0.
findings.attack: The integration block should be a real test with exact assertions and cleanup fixture.
findings.defense: The query itself is real SQLite integration rather than a fake DB.

findings.title: TAGLINE_PROMISE_TIMEOUT_ORDER_AND_RESUMPTION_UNEARNED
findings.evidence: Public/source tagline promises encoding, cardinality, order, timeout and resumption; theory executes only basic Unicode normalization and a pair query plus deterministic sorting.
findings.impact: Learner can complete theory without ever proving timeout or checkpoint resumption.
findings.attack: Add explicit failure-injection tests for timeout and persistent checkpoint restart.
findings.defense: Some of these dimensions may be exercised in later I Do/practice content outside LESSONS_ONLY scope.

findings.title: NO_REAL_E2E_INGEST_TO_PAIRS_TO_REVIEW
findings.evidence: T4-A defines E2E as ingest→pairs→review, but canonical theory only creates a SQLite table and query.
findings.impact: The distinction between integration and E2E is described but not demonstrated.
findings.attack: Run a synthetic record through validation, persistence, candidate generation and review artifact creation.
findings.defense: Roadmap increment emphasizes a suite, and a minimal integration example need not also be full E2E.

findings.title: FLAKY_BAD_IS_EFFECTIVELY_A_TAUTOLOGY_NOT_A_FLAKE
findings.evidence: random.random()>0.0 almost always true and datetime.now().microsecond>=0 is always true.
findings.impact: The canonical anti-pattern almost never exhibits the intermittent failure it claims to model.
findings.attack: Use an actually intermittent predicate or better, an order/time-dependent deterministic reproducer.
findings.defense: It visually contains two uncontrolled dependencies and is labeled anti-pattern.

findings.title: FLAKE_RATE_GATE_HAS_NO_MEASUREMENT_CONTRACT
findings.evidence: Prose says job fails if flake_rate>0 but defines no repeated-run population, window, denominator or quarantine treatment.
findings.impact: A metric can be reported or gamed without a reproducible definition.
findings.attack: Define attempts/runs/test set/window and distinguish first-run failure from retry recovery.
findings.defense: Zero flakes is an aspirational gate and details could live in CI tooling.

findings.title: STABLE_HELPER_RESEEDS_GLOBAL_RNG_AND_CAN_COUPLE_TESTS
findings.evidence: stable(seed) calls random.seed(seed) on the module generator every invocation.
findings.impact: Tests executed after it may observe a reset random sequence.
findings.attack: Use rng=random.Random(seed) local to the helper/fixture.
findings.defense: The example is single-process and intentionally demonstrates deterministic output.

findings.title: CONTRACT_TEST_TERMINOLOGY_REMAINS_AMBIGUOUS
findings.evidence: Outcome says contract tests of borders while prose mostly means behavioral input/output tests; provider-consumer compatibility is not distinguished.
findings.impact: Learner can carry an overloaded meaning into service/API testing.
findings.attack: Name behavioral contracts/spec tests separately from interface/provider-consumer contract tests.
findings.defense: The local section context consistently uses contract as executable behavior, so readers can infer the intended sense.

rejected_findings.claim: Hypothesis shrinking is invalid or outdated
rejected_findings.reason: Current Hypothesis 6.167.1 explicitly includes shrinking as a normal phase.

rejected_findings.claim: Using SQLite in-memory is inherently invalid for integration testing
rejected_findings.reason: The section honestly limits SQLite to local schema/query logic and says a real container/dialect is needed later.

rejected_findings.claim: Hand-written fakes are always inferior to mocks
rejected_findings.reason: Stateful fakes are often appropriate; the issue is interface parity and test scope, not the existence of fakes.
Fixed seeds are useful for determinism/reproduction; the defect is relying on one global fixed sample as the whole exploration strategy.

rejected_findings.claim: Golden snapshots are inherently bad tests
rejected_findings.reason: Goldens can be valuable when versioned, canonicalized and review-gated; S28's problem is that those controls are only narrated.

usable: idempotence and symmetry are useful when explicitly part of the API contract
metamorphic relations can serve as oracles when exact outputs are unknown
golden changes should not auto-accept silently
over-mocking pure logic is usually counterproductive
SQLite can be a limited local integration layer when its limits are stated
flake retries are not a substitute for root-cause repair
